description: A digital delay of as much as 3 seconds, with a feedback path, a send and return insert point, and a crossfade that covers changes of delay time

params.text: Sets the delay time as the cube of the dial across a 3 second buffer; with a cable in CLK it picks a ratio of the clock period instead
Sets how much of the delayed signal is written back into the delay line, -1 to +1, with negative settings inverting it on the way round
Scales what the time CV input does to the delay time, from fully inverted through nothing to fully positive
Scales what the feedback CV input does to the feedback amount, from fully inverted through nothing to fully positive
Crossfades the output between the dry input and the delayed signal

inputs.text: Shifts the delay time by a fifth of its voltage, scaled by its attenuverter
Shifts the feedback amount by a fifth of its voltage, scaled by its attenuverter
A clock here takes the delay time away from the knob: the knob then picks a ratio of the measured clock period, from an eighth of it up to double
What gets written into the delay line, in place of the input and feedback sum; with nothing patched the delay feeds itself as usual
The signal into the delay; a polyphonic cable is summed down to one channel

outputs.text: The input added to the feedback signal, which is what the module would write into the delay line
The dry input and the delayed signal mixed in the proportion D/W sets

notes: the module is monophonic: the input is summed to one channel and both outputs carry one channel
SEND and RET form an insert: patch SEND out to an effect and its result back into RET, and the effect is placed inside the feedback loop
a clock needs two rising edges before the module can measure its period; the knob sets the delay time directly until that second edge arrives
with a cable in CLK the delay time knob selects from sixteen ratios of the clock period, an eighth to double in steps of an eighth
below the middle of the delay time dial the clock ratio is squared, which spreads the short divisions further apart
changing the delay time crossfades between two read points in the buffer rather than sweeping one, so the pitch of the delayed signal does not slide
everything written into the delay line passes through a DC blocking filter and is inverted on the way in, so a repeat comes back with its polarity flipped
bypassing the module passes IN straight through to OUT

inputs.0:
±5V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 1V.
inputs.1:
±5V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
inputs.2:
high above 0V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.3:
continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads the input plus the feedback signal.
